samples.summary: Rejecting an *empty* segment turns the ordinary "no workspace configured" state into a cryptic "Invalid identifier" failure on every command — behaviour beyond the encoding/preview-fidelity goal of this change
samples.evidence: `resolveConfig` deliberately defaults `workspace` to `''` in all four resolution branches (packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:99-100,124-126,145-147,161-164), and config.ts:108 documents the resulting `/workspaces//...` 404 as the expected outcome of an unresolved workspace. With `seg('')` now throwing, an unauthenticated/unconfigured user gets `Invalid identifier "": a URL path segment cannot be empty…` from every namespace instead of a 404 or a message pointing at `login` / `ctx use`. The empty-segment rule is also not required by the traversal problem the change is solving (only the dot-segment rule is), so it is unrequested scope with a user-visible UX cost.

finding.summary: Rejection throws a bare `Error`, so the new input-validation failure surfaces under the generic `ERROR` code instead of a stable one, contradicting the CLI's documented error-code contract
finding.evidence: `docs/design/cli.md` §8.1 (lines 767–807) states that argument-parsing/bad-input failures are "part of that contract, not an exception to it" and are enveloped under the stable code `USAGE`; `outputError`/`errorCode` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:42-47) falls back to `'ERROR'` when the thrown Error carries no `code`. The new `seg()` throws `new Error('Invalid identifier …')` with no `code`, so `wafflebase api-keys revoke ..` emits `{"error":{"code":"ERROR",…}}` — an unstable code for exactly the class of user-input failure the design doc says agents should be able to branch on. §8.2's new paragraph documents the rejection but never says what code or exit code it produces.
searchedFor: grep for USAGE / stable error codes in packages/cli/src

verdict.reason: The finding's premise — that the CLI's documented error-code contract requires a stable code for user-input failures — is contradicted by the docs themselves. docs/design/cli.md:782-788 scopes `USAGE` explicitly and only to commander parse failures ("Commander exits during parsing… reaches runCli's catch as a CommanderError, which envelopes it under the stable code USAGE"), which is exactly how packages/cli/src/cli.ts:51-88 implements it; `seg()` throws inside an action handler, outside that clause. packages/cli/README.md:116-122 states the full contract: typed errors carry command-specific codes, argument-parsing failures report `USAGE`, and "everything else reports \"ERROR\"" — so `ERROR` is the documented outcome, not an unstable deviation. The only cross-cutting guarantee for bad input is the exit code (cli.md:805-807, "Agents can branch on the exit code without parsing the error body"), and outputError sets exitCode 1 (formatter.ts:62), asserted in test/read-dry-run.test.ts:304-311. Multiple pre-existing input validations throw bare Error the same way (docs/page-range.ts:76, commands/sheets-import.ts:15, commands/notes.ts:197, commands/slides.ts:204), so seg() follows the established pattern. The rejection is also documented in the design doc (cli.md:851-857), and the originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260816-cli-dry-run-read-commands-todo.md:50-60) has no error-code acceptance criterion and lists "no output-shape change" as a Non-goal. A dedicated code would be a taste improvement (minor), not a spec-conformance failure.

finding.summary: URL construction for the api-keys management routes is duplicated in the command layer instead of reused from HttpClient. `apiKeysUrl()` re-derives `${server}/workspaces/${seg(workspace)}/api-keys[/:id]`, which HttpClient already builds in three places (listApiKeys/createApiKey/revokeApiKey). The whole point of the change is that "the preview is the request", yet the preview now depends on a hand-copied mirror that can silently drift (e.g. if the route ever moves under /api/v1). A single exported URL builder on HttpClient (or a dry-run mode on the client) would make the guarantee structural rather than by comment.
finding.evidence: function apiKeysUrl(opts, keyId?) { const base = `${server}/workspaces/${seg(config.workspace)}/api-keys`; ... } — duplicating http-client.ts lines ~404-417

verdict.reason: The alleged duplication is not present. `apiKeysUrl` is defined exactly once, in the shared module packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:60-63, and is imported by both consumers: packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:5,15-17 (previewUrl simply forwards to it) and packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:8, where listApiKeys/createApiKey/revokeApiKey call apiKeysUrl at lines 386, 392, 402 rather than constructing the path themselves. A repo-wide grep of packages/cli/src for `apiKeysUrl|workspaces/${` finds no second definition of the route, so there is no hand-copied mirror that can drift; the "single exported URL builder" the finding asks for already exists. The evidence quoted by the reviewer (a local `function apiKeysUrl(opts, keyId?)` in the command layer) does not appear in the command file, which takes a `config` from the shared builder instead.
